result.title: Swap, Replicate, Read the Mass: A Protocol for Auditing Demographic Bias in System One Decision Models
result.summary: System One decision models replace text generation with typed, probability-scored answers and are entering production. Answers execute without a person in the loop, and no multi-model audit exists on established bias benchmarks. We provide that audit: three benchmarks: BBQ (all eleven categories), CrowS-Pairs, and SilverSpoon, adapted to the typed interface, twelve models plus a no-thinking ablation, and 1,638,000 decisions. Every order-sensitive item runs twice with options swapped; native typed models also swap labels; ten configurations repeat under extra seeds and batch 16. We find widespread stereotype alignment, order-dependent answers, and confidence that tracks instability rather than bias. In BBQ, 97 of 143 model-by-category scores are significant and 94 aligned, while the commercial reference abstains on 99.5% of ambiguous items, hiding aligned probability mass. Option swaps flip 0.0% to 72.6% of choices; typed scoring stays below 10% except Laya (22-33%), and untuned letter prompting reaches 73%. CrowS-Pairs preference spans 0.496 to 0.816, and boolean answers can be decided by position (1.00 versus 0.005). SilverSpoon judgments shift toward lower-SES labels in five of eight decision models, inherited from the 9B backbone or induced by tuning. Audits must permute options and reverse questions by default; order-invariant scoring should become a procurement requirement.

AI.brief_summary: 论文对十二个 System One 决策模型（typed、概率打分答案接口）在 BBQ、CrowS-Pairs 与 SilverSpoon 上做偏见审计，共约 163.8 万次决策，并系统交换选项顺序、更换种子与批大小，报告刻板印象对齐、顺序依赖以及置信度与实际稳定性脱钩。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「交换选项、反转问题、检查被隐藏的概率质量」的审计协议可供核查 LVR 答案是否真正依赖内部证据；「置信度跟随不稳定性而非偏见」的发现也可能提示 STOP 决策中置信信号不可靠，迁移是否成立仍需判断。
